statement: A ruling is only usable by a later session if it can be quoted from a durable artefact.
evidence: I-43; RETRO1_rulings_timeline.csv (106 identifiers, 1 with no dated evidence at all)
mechanism: Sessions share no memory. An assertion whose source cannot be retrieved cannot be distinguished by the next session from one that was never issued.

statement: Rulings are issued during runs, not before them: the instruction side is not where a ruling first appears.
evidence: RETRO1_rulings_timeline.csv: 101 REACTIVE, 1 PRE_REGISTERED, 3 GOVERNANCE_FIRST, 1 UNRESOLVED of 106
mechanism: A spec's 'rulings in force' list restates rulings already issued elsewhere; no artefact exists in which a ruling is written before the run it governs, so every ruling enters the record as a correction.

statement: A fact crossing the chat-to-disk boundary loses its provenance and arrives as an assertion.
evidence: I-40, I-43, I-48, I-58; RETRO-1 section 2.1 (13 chat exports on disk, none of them the design-seat/CC dialogue, which has zero exports)
mechanism: The chat side is not version-controlled, so a receiving artefact has nothing to cite. The existing remedy - cite the number_id, never the value - covers numbers and not rulings, quoted documents or prior context.

statement: A substring check matches the record of a correction as though it were the error.
evidence: I-47 / Ruling AK; lint run 11 Aug 2026: 3 of 4 or_ignore hits are comments PROHIBITING INSERT OR IGNORE, and several magic_number hits are comments documenting the derivation
mechanism: The project writes corrections visibly - superseding headers, '(was X)' notes, retained superseded values - so any check matching a fragment finds the prohibited token inside the text that prohibits it. The convention and the failure mode are the same design choice.

statement: An advisory control is not a control.
evidence: RETRO1_gates_and_controls.csv: hash_order reports 127 violations and enforces 0; lint_baseline.json suppresses pre-T5 debt so the lint fails on NEW violations only
mechanism: A check that cannot fail the run changes no behaviour, so it is read exactly like a check that passes.

statement: A persisted verdict cannot notice that it has aged; only a live query can report absence.
evidence: I-42; TRACE-1 section 5: figure_asset.path_exists reads 1 on 7 rows eleven days after the files moved; raster_asset clean at 0 of 192
mechanism: A stored boolean has no trigger to revisit itself. It can record presence at write time and has no mechanism to record a later absence.

statement: Registration confers no test coverage, and nothing enforces the second step after the first.
evidence: TRACE-1 four-way split: 43 numbers have a producer and no test; T8 went from 14 drifted of 71 to 72 of 153 as the registry grew
mechanism: The registrar and the reproduction test are separate scripts with no link between them, so the recompute function does not grow when the registry does.

statement: A number can be computed in a session and registered without any producer being committed.
evidence: I-29; TRACE-1: 21 s11_* rows where the string appears in no tracked file of any kind, and their decided_by cites an untracked draft; the spat1_* batch was in the same state for hours
mechanism: Nothing in the registration path requires a committed producer, so a value held only in a session's context can be written to the registry and the session can then end.

statement: A spec can cite a document that does not exist, and both seats will reason from the citation.
evidence: I-48; RETRO1_spec_inventory.csv: 36 of 113 specs carry at least one absent citation, 73 absent citations in total
mechanism: Citations are written from memory of the repository rather than checked against it, and nothing in the authoring path resolves them.

statement: The exit code is not the check; only querying the result is.
evidence: I-60 surfaces 1 and 2; the INVENTORY-1 staging check that errored inside a pipeline while the chain continued and the commit proceeded unverified
mechanism: A pipeline returns the status of its last stage, and a shell chain continues on it, so an upstream check that could not run is indistinguishable from one that passed.

statement: Where a re-run's cause is not required by the report format, it goes unrecorded.
evidence: RETRO-1 section 3.4: 33 of 104 reports showing a re-run state no cause
mechanism: No section of the run-report convention requires stating what preceded a re-run, so the cause survives only when the author happens to narrate it.

statement: Specs in this corpus range from 23 to 637 lines with no association to reactive-ruling count or re-run count established by this extraction.
evidence: RETRO1_spec_inventory.csv: median 149 lines; the association was not computed because the reactive-ruling keying is at task grain and most specs carry 0-3

statement: Four recurring spec sections appear in a minority of specs: checks-on-checks 3, what-this-is-not 5, rulings-in-force 10, spine-anchor 10, of 113.
mechanism: NO_MECHANISM - presence was measurable, but whether a run RESPONDED to a section was not, so 'decorative' is not established by this extraction. See the coverage note in the report.

statement: A gate's firing cannot be established from the corpus by text search.
evidence: RETRO1_gates_and_controls.csv: 316 gates; a first proximity-free test marked 299 as having fired, which was a coincidence test; tightened to 500-character proximity it marks 265
mechanism: NO_MECHANISM - reports do not record gate outcomes in any consistent form, so neither number is evidence. Only the hand-verified firings in the report body are.

statement: Checking rather than complying catches design-seat errors, and the corpus records it working.
evidence: Ruling BE (my 'two different measurements' claim withdrawn on the design seat's challenge); TRACE-1 (spec said 142 rows, registry held 143 then 156); RETRO-1 (spec said chat exports may be absent - 13 were present, but of a different interface)
mechanism: Both seats write from partial and time-lagged views of a repository that several sessions are changing at once, so a stated premise is a claim about the past. Verifying it costs one query and is the only way the error surfaces before it propagates.
